rows: A tornado destroyed 5 mobile homes and damaged an additional 20 homes just east of China. Trees and power lines were blown down.
Lamar University recorded 69 mph wind gust.
Jefferson County Sheriff Office reported a power pole blown down east of China.
A roof was blown off an auto sales company on Fannett Road at Highway 69.
A 58 mph wind gust was record at the Sabine Pass North station.
Power lines were blown down near Lamar University.
Trees and power lines were blown down in Nederland.
Power lines blown down near Highway 105 and Major Drive. Reported by TV station in Beaumont.
An industrial plant along the Neches River ESE of Beaumont reported penny size hail.
A Beaumont TV station reported nickel size hail in Bevil Oaks.
A Beaumont TV station reported ping pong ball size hail in Bevil Oaks.
The KBPT ASOS measured a wind gust of 73 mph from a localized microburst. No damage was reported at the Southeast Texas Regional Airport.
A trained spotter estimated 65 mph winds in Port Arthur.
Beaumont Enterprise reported numerous downed powerlines across Beaumont, with 5700 customers without power across the city and 11000 customers without power throughout southeast Texas.

An EF1 Tornado touched down just west of the Kohls Department Store in the Parkdale Mall area. The tornado struck the Kohls, tearing off part of its roof and collapsing the front entrance. Damage to the store forced it to close for several weeks. The tornado continued to the nort…
KFDM-TV reported penny size hail near Parkdale Mall.

An NWS Storm Survey found a low-end EF1 tornado struck the eastern part of Nome. The tornado began southwest of Rodeo Drive in the southeast part of Nome and moved north-northeast, causing minor damage to a rodeo arena. Several outbuildings were then damaged or destroyed on the w…

The public and local media reported the tin metal roof was blown off Snowden Automotive on South MLK Jr. Parkway at Calder Road in downtown Beaumont, injuring one person and damaging several cars in the parking lot.
KFDM-TV reported trees blown down on Helbig Road, with more than 4400 customers losing power in Jefferson County.
KFDM-TV reported trees blown down on Carpenter Road.
Port Arthur Daily News reported large tree branches blown down in Port Arthur.
Southeast Texas Regional Airport ASOS measured a wind gust of 60 mph.
Entergy reported over 1000 customers without power across Jefferson County, particularly in the Labelle and Hillebrandt communities.
Public reported pea to dime size hail near Lamar University.
Public reported small tree limbs down with an estimated wind gust of 55 mph.
Dime sized hail was reported in Groves and it lasted for about 5 minutes.
A public report was received of hail to the size of quarters.
Penny sized hail was reported near China via facebook.
A report was relayed through Facebook of hail mostly nickel sized with some quarter sized mixed in.
A severe thunderstorm moved southeast across Jefferson County and into Sea Rim State Park producing a wind gust of 57 MPH.
Nickel sized hail was reported in Bevel Oaks. The small hail lasted for about 8 minutes.
Several trees and many tree limbs were blown down or broken around Groves. One tree fell on a house.
Thunderstorms passed across Beaumont producing wind gusts to around 60 MPH along with small hail to pea size.
A report of large hail was received by the Beaumont Police Department during the afternoon of the 3rd, however the hail size was later determined to be the size of nickels.
A wind gust of 66 MPH was recorded at the Jack Brooks Regional Airport with a passing severe storm.
One inch in diameter hail was reported near Winnie.
One inch in diameter hail was reported in Beaumont.
Golf ball size hail was reported in Port Acres.
A report was relayed by Beaumont media of penny to quarter sized hail in Nederland.
A picture was received through Facebook of hail of half dollar size near Port Arthur.
Multiple trees were downed around Van Buren Elementary and nearby streets in Groves.
The Beaumont Police Department reported three quarter inch hail.
A wind gust of around 70 MPH was reported with a thunderstorm.
A tree fell and partially damaged 2 homes and a carport and car in North Beaumont. A few other isolated trees were also reported down in the area.

Broadcast media shared a video of a brief tornado that occurred in a field. The tornado moved roughly half a mile through the field causing no damage. Multiple reports funnel clouds were also received from this storm.
A picture was sent in of a free standing metal tower bent from winds during a thunderstorm.
Mostly dime size hail, however a few quarters also mixed in during a thunderstorm.
KBMT reports an estimated wind gust of 60 MPH on Major Drive in Beaumont.
KBMT relayed a report of trees down at Sul Ross and Williamsburg in the Regina Howell area of Beaumont.
KBMT relayed a report of quarter size hail near Port Neches.
Quarter size hail was reported between Winnie and Nome.
Roof damage from a thunderstorm was reported to a law office and an apartment complex near Central Mall.

At Lamar University, strong winds uplifted and peeled back a large portion of the University Police station and toppled several large trees. A glass wall and several windows were also blown in. On Oregon Ave, the exterior brick wall of an apartment building collapsed. Max estimat…
Multiple reports of quarter size hail was reported along Major Drive in Beaumont.
A report of golf ball size was reported in Beaumont.
A home received roof damage from a thunderstorm near the intersection of Bluebonnet and Richmond Avenues in Port Arthur.
Multiple videos taken around Port Arthur and Groves indicated a landspout briefly occurred near Sabine Lake and Pleasure Island. No damage was noted.
Pictures from social media indicated a landspout briefly occurred in a rice field 2 miles south of China. No damage was reported.
Quarter sized hail was reported in Bevil Oaks.
The ASOS at Jack Brooks Regional Airport recorded a 58 MPH wind gust.
Several trees were blown down in the Bevil Oaks community some of which damaged homes.
Multiple trees were downed in the La Belle area.
Several large tree limbs were down at a residence in Beaumont.
A tree was downed by a thunderstorm.
Minor roof damage was done to a home near Jack Brooks Regional Airport.

South of Fannett, an area of a strong thunderstorms began bowing out leading to an increase in velocities. Tree damage began to become increasingly evident in a width extending from around Boondocks Road south of Fannett to just north of FM 365. Tree damage continued to be noted …
Tree branches around 3 inches thick and power poles were broken in Nederland.
A dock crane was blown over into the Neches Ship Channel. A large salvage crane also broke loose.
KBPT ASOS recorded a wind gust of 52 knots.
Personal weather station recorded a wind gust of 60 mph in groves.
The ASOS at Jack Brooks Regional Airport (KBPT) recorded a wind gust of 60 kts or 69 mph.
One inch in diameter hail reported via social media.
KBMT 12 relayed a report of trees downed near China.
The public and local media reported damage to an aluminum carport, the roof at Grand Slam Carwash on College and 23rd, and multiple trees down in the area with one landing on a home on Broadway.
A tree was downed on to a home.
Winds blew down fencing and a utility pole.
Multiple RVs were blown over at an RV park. One person suffered minor injuries.
A heat burst produced strong wind gusts that damaged a garage near Jack Brooks Regional Airport.

A brief tornado started just west of Nick Ave in Port Acres where there was damage to out buildings and caused some roof damage to homes. The tornado moved northeast crossing Silver Ave then curved north northeast crossing 63 street before dissipating near 64th Street. Numerous l…
Media reported roof damage to a business in Nederland.
A few homes had minor roof damage, however one home had the roof destroyed. Numerous trees were downed or had large limbs broken. Fences were also down in the area.
KBPT recorded a wind gust of 67 mph.

Numerous videos and pictures were received through social media of a slow moving waterspout moving from Sabine Lake into Motiva. The land spout produced no noticeable damage beyond tipping over trash cans.
A flagpole was snapped and leaning on a home.
Multiple homes suffered damage from high wind gusts.

An EF-1 tornado touched down just south of Highway 73, and tracked into the Taylor Landing community. Weak damage to roofs were common, along with uprooted trees and destroyed privacy fences. The tornado ended somewhere in the Taylor Bayou marsh downstream from Taylor Landing. Ma…
Power poles were snapped in Beauxart Gardens. Southeast Texas Regional Airport also recorded a wind gust of 55 mph.
A mesonet site recorded a wind gust of 64 mph.
A large tree was downed onto a roof in Port Acres.
A picture of hail ranging from quarters to golf ball size was received through social media.
An MPING report of hail to 1 inch in diameter.
One inch hail near Ford Park.
A softwood tree was split in half.
A large branch was broken off a tree.
A wind gust of 68 MPH was recorded at the Pietzsch-Macarthur School by a KFDM mesonet. A building was also damaged at Gladys City.
Trees and powerlines were downed in Beaumont. One tree fell onto a car on 5th Street.
A KFDM mesonet site recorded a wind gust of 60mph.
A Tempest weather station recorded a wind gust of 63 mph.
A photo of hail was sent in through social media. Most hail was around dime sized however a few quarter sized stones were mixed in.
A tree was downed along 7100 Tram Road in Beaumont.
A photo of half dollar sized hail was receive from near Bevil Oaks.
A trailer was overturned due to a high wind gust at the South Texas State Fair at Ford Park.

A NWS storm survey revealed that an EF-2 tornado impacted areas of Port Arthur. The tornado began near the intersection of 17th Street and Savannah Ave southeast of Motiva. The tornado path traveled east, peaking out near the Progressive Missionary Baptist Church where a large po…
Broadcast media relayed reports of minor damage to commercial buildings along with power poles and lines downed.
A microburst produced high winds at the Jack Brooks Regional Airport. In neighboring portions of Nederland numerous trees and powerlines were also downed.
Several pictures of large hail were received through social media from Hampshire.
Ping pong ball sized hail reported in Fannett.
A helicopter was spun around and a boarding stairway was blown down the tarmac. The KBPT ASOS registered a wind gust of 56 mph before the sensor stopped reporting.
A report of three quarter to one inch hail was received from Port Arthur.
Golf ball to hen egg size hail was reported around Groves.
A wind gust of 73 mph was recorded on an Ambient Weather Station.
A wind gust of 51 knots was recorded at PORT2.

An EF-3 tornado developed south of Houston and moved across Chambers County into Jefferson County just south of Russel Road. It snapped off power poles at French Rd before continuing northeast. An area of trees were snapped off and uprooted just south of the Big Hill Strategic Oi…

Six RVs were flipped along the west bank of Sabine Lake on Pleasure Island. Two people were injured. This was caused by strong winds flowing into the approaching tornadic supercell that would pass to the south of the RV park.
Golf ball size hail was reported at the Pleasure Island RV resort just before winds flipped multiple RVs.
A weathernet station recorded a wind gust of 83 mph at the Sabine Pass School.
A flag pole was broken by high winds.
